title: Geometric Decoupling: Diagnosing the Structural Instability of Latent
claim: Normal generations place curvature on genuine fine detail, while out-of-distribution generations concentrate extreme curvature on unstable semantic conflicts rather than perceptible detail.
layout: 3x2 grid of triplets; normal left, OOD right; image, LC-map, PHFE-map
description: A 3-row by 2-column grid of subfigures. Each subfigure has three square panels: a generated image, its Local Complexity map (LC-Map), and its Projected High-Frequency Energy map (PHFE-Map). The left column shows normal samples: (a) a chicken, (c) a chair, (e) a penguin. The right column shows OOD counterparts: (b) a chicken with teeth, (d) a melting chair, (f) a flying penguin. The maps use a jet colormap, with deep blue for low values and red for high values. In normal samples, red is sparse and tracks object edges and detail. In OOD samples, large red clusters cover semantically conflicting regions such as the teeth, the melting seat and the wings. The LC and PHFE maps match less closely there. Italic captions sit under each subfigure. The eye goes first to the vivid heatmaps and the odd OOD images.
caption: Qualitative Visualization of Geometric Decoupling. We display Normal (a,c,e) and OOD (b,d,f) samples alongside their Local Complexity Maps (LC-Map) and Projected High-Frequency Energy Maps (PHFE-Map). In each subfigure, from left to right: the Generated Image, the LC-Map, and the PHFE-Map. Red regions in the LC-Map denote "Geometric Hotspots" of extreme curvature. This spatial correspondence confirms that the model allocates its maximum geometric complexity to resolving semantic conflicts, often decoupling from the actual high-frequency detail (PHFE), thereby illustrating the misallocation of geometric resources. The more examples please check Appendix. [ref].
abstract: Latent Diffusion Models (LDMs) achieve high-fidelity synthesis but suffer from latent space brittleness, causing discontinuous semantic jumps during editing. We introduce a Riemannian framework to diagnose this instability by analyzing the generative Jacobian, decomposing geometry into \textit{Local Scaling} (capacity) and \textit{Local Complexity} (curvature). Our study uncovers a \textbf{``Geometric Decoupling"}: while curvature in normal generation functionally encodes image detail, OOD generation exhibits a functional decoupling where extreme curvature is wasted on unstable semantic boundaries rather than perceptible details. This geometric misallocation identifies ``Geometric Hotspots" as the structural root of instability, providing a robust intrinsic metric for diagnosing generative reliability.
